subject.title: [Bug]: `exec` tool does not inherit `skills.entries.*.env` environment variables

question: Should OpenClaw automatically allow credential-shaped keys from `skills.entries.<skill>.env` into host exec, or require a narrower skill-owned credential delivery contract first?
rationale: The reported bug is real, but the obvious fix changes which executable child processes can receive secrets and conflicts with the open generic-exec secret-leak boundary in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/78528.

options.title: Design the skill-owned boundary
options.body: Preserve the user-visible skill env contract, but route credentials only to intended skill/plugin execution paths and strip them from unrelated generic exec children.

options.title: Allow explicit config env broadly
options.body: Treat operator-configured `skills.entries.<skill>.env` as consent to pass sensitive names into all host exec during that run, while still blocking dangerous host env names.

options.title: Patch bundled gog metadata only
options.body: Add declared env metadata for `GOG_ACCOUNT` and `GOG_KEYRING_PASSWORD` as a narrow bundled-skill repair, leaving arbitrary sensitive config keys blocked.

recommendation.title: Design the skill-owned boundary
recommendation.body: Preserve the user-visible skill env contract, but route credentials only to intended skill/plugin execution paths and strip them from unrelated generic exec children.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans SecretRef handling and host exec env hardening, both areas tied to this person's recent commit history.
